title: Chuck McClendon and the raise request to Harold Logan
summary: Story of a sideman asking Lloyd Price's manager for a raise and being told to move bands.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And you know, like some of those guys, now when I asked, one time I, I forgot what band it was for a raise, and he told me, and I knew that he was making it, because he had just come out with a new record and it was hot. I said, I think it's time for me to get a raise. Oh man, I can't give you no raise now. I said, I might be able to give you. I said, when are you going to give me a raise? He said, but two months from now, I'll be able to give you a raise. I said, well, here's my two weeks' notice. Now when you can get enough money to pay me what I want, then you can call me. But man, a lot of those guys in those bands like that, they're afraid to act for a raise. Because if really, they might get fired. Like when I was playing with Lloyd Price Band, Chuck McClendon wanted a raise, but he didn't want to ask Lloyd for a raise, because Lloyd didn't handle the business. Lloyd's manager handled the business.

Harold Logan. So Chuck, they had a part of the band. We were at the Royal Theater in Baltimore, and it was a big opening. So Logan decided to treat the band to some drinks at a club down the street from the Royal. So Logan didn't drink, but he had a few drinks that night, because everybody was happy, because the opening night was so great. So Chuck said, well, here's my time to get a raise. So he wouldn't say, hey, Logan, baby, look, I want to talk with you. He said, yeah, Chuck, what you got on mind, man? Have a drink. Yeah, man. Yeah, I said, look, man, you know, I've been with the band a long time, you know, and I was thinking of getting a, it was time for me to get a raise. He said, okay, well, we'll talk about it tomorrow. Chuck said, told him, yeah, man, I'm going to get a raise tomorrow. Oh, Logan was feeling good, I caught him at the right time. So he sent for Chuck the next day. He said, Chuck, I was thinking about what you were asking for. You know something? You really deserve a raise, but I can't give you a raise. You get with another band.
Yeah, go to another band. And he'll be acting for what you want, then maybe you'll, but you'll be fired now. Oh man, I'll, you know.
